subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.

spec.name: Hover Technical
spec.description: A militarized pickup truck converted to ride on four glowing hover thrusters, low-poly cyberpunk with neon trim, armor plates and a bed-mounted weapon.
spec.layout: A boxy pickup hovering about 0.45 m above the floor on four ducted thrusters that replace the wheels (one at each corner, wheel-arch positions). The front (+Z) has a sloped armored hood with a bull-bar, slit headlights and a cyan neon strip. The cab sits mid-length with a sloped windshield, side windows and a roll cage with a light bar on the roof. Behind it is an open cargo bed with a swivel gun mount, ammo crates and a rear bumper with a tail thruster. Palette is dark gunmetal hull, hazard-yellow trim, neon cyan and magenta glow on thrusters and underglow, with panelled/worn paints, decals (stripes, serial numbers, kanji/glyph signs) and glowing parts for lights, thruster cores and screens. Everything is faceted: boxes, wedges, extrudes and low-segment lathes. Only the thrusters touch no floor: the hull floats and the lowest points are the thruster bottoms at about y=0.

parts.builds: Underframe and lower hull: a slab chassis with skirt armor panels along both sides (panelled gunmetal paint, hazard-yellow stripe decals), front sloped hood with vents and a bull-bar bumper with magenta-lit slits, a rear bumper, glowing cyan underglow strips along the underside, and fender arches over each thruster position (arches only, not the thrusters). Includes the hood wedge ahead of the cab up to z=2.65 and the bed's outer side walls and tailgate from z=-0.9 to z=-2.65 (low-poly slab walls with ribbing and worn paint). Headlights as glowing warm slits, tail lights glowing red.
parts.attaches: Cab sits on cabFloor/chassisTop; bed interior and gun sit at bedFloor/gunPivot; thrusters hang from the four thruster mounts below the arches.

parts.builds: Passenger cabin from z=-0.9 to z=1.0, y=0.95..1.9: a faceted armored cab with sloped windshield and rear window (glass colour with a faint glowing HUD-glyph texture), side windows with armor slats, doors with handles and a hazard stripe, a roof with a roll-cage frame of rods, a glowing light bar (warm and cyan) across the front of the roof, a roof antenna and a small glowing sign decal with cyberpunk glyph text. Mirrors on both sides. Simple dashboard and two seat shapes visible through the glass.
parts.attaches: Rests on cabFloor / chassisTop; the hood of the chassis meets its front at z=1.0; the bed begins behind at z=-0.9.

parts.builds: Four hover thruster pods, one per thruster mount, each on its own joint: a lathe-turned faceted duct (8-sided) with a metal-dark outer shell and yellow hazard ring, a glowing cyan thrusterCore disc inside the bottom with a magenta rim ring, internal fan blades (extruded, 6 per pod), strut arms (rods and plates) connecting each pod up to the chassis arch, small exhaust fins and a glowing downward cone/glow card for the thrust. Pods are about 0.9 m wide and the bottom of each rests at y=0 to 0.02. Also a smaller tail thruster pod centred on bumperRear (rigid on body joint) with a glowing core.
parts.attaches: Each pod is centred on its thrusterXX mount and its strut meets the chassis arch underside at y=0.85; tail pod mounts at bumperRear.

parts.builds: Everything inside and above the open cargo bed between z=-2.6 and z=-0.9: bed floor with ribbed panelled plating, ammo crates (olive crate colour with stencil decals and yellow straps), a fuel drum pair, coiled cable rods, a roll bar behind the cab, and the swivel-mounted heavy weapon on gunYaw/gunPitch: pedestal, ring base, yoke, a boxy receiver with a cyan glowing energy cell, long barrel with a shroud, muzzle brake, ammo belt of small spheres/boxes feeding from a box magazine, shield plate with magenta glowing slit sight. Neon cyan strip lights on bed rails and a small holo-screen card on the gun.
parts.attaches: Floor at bedFloor (y=0.95) between the chassis side walls; gun base at gunPivot with joints gunYaw and gunPitch; roll bar leans against the rear of the cab at z=-0.9.

calls.reasoning:
I'll write the buildThrusters function using the Ctx type from the module, positioning the pods centered on the mounts at roughly x=±1.05, z=1.6/-1.5, with their base at y=0.

I'm shaping the pod geometry as lathed profiles—an outer shell wall flaring from a narrow base to a wider mid-section, plus a thin hazard-trim ring band and a magenta accent ring near the bottom, defining each as a closed outline of radius/height points to feed into the lathe builder.

I'm then adding a core glow disc, a hub cylinder, and a set of six flat horizontal fan blades, each defined by a small quadrilateral cross-section extruded along a radial direction with vertical thickness, topped off with a downward glow cone.

I'm also planning a floor-level glow ring beneath the duct (using concentric stroked rings for an alpha-cut radial effect) plus a small upward glow cone tucked inside the duct beneath the fan, and now I'm working out strut placements connecting the pod shell to the underside of the arch at inward-angled positions.

Now I'm adding a mounting plate box and small radial outer-shell fins, then moving on to designing the tail pod duct at the rear bumper, oriented horizontally along the z-axis.

Setting up bone joints for each pod so they attach correctly, picking colors from the palette (metal dark, trim, neon magenta/cyan, thruster core), and deciding to use painted countershading rather than glow for the main hull shell to keep it visually distinct from the glowing thruster parts.

Working out part counts per pod—shell, ring, rimring, core, hub, six blades, four fins, two struts, plate, cone, floor card—roughly 20 parts each, times four pods plus the tail. Defining the fin shape as an extruded outline placed radially around the pod, and the floor card as a textured plane with glowing concentric cyan rings facing upward. Now setting joint hinge positions for the thruster mounts.

I'll use the provided Ctx type without redeclaring it, and keep the module compact at around 100 parts. I'm sketching a box helper function that wraps the part-creation API for positioning, sizing, and coloring.

Now I'm laying out the truck bed geometry—floor slab dimensions, panelled paint pulled from the clockwork kit, floor ribs, crates with strap decals, fuel drums, and a roll bar behind the cab. I'm also working through gun placement and barrel length so it clears the cab roof without colliding.

Shield goes near the receiver protecting the gunner, and I'll orient the barrel along -Z using a cylinder with a backward direction vector. Crates sit at x ±0.6, z -1.2 with dimensions roughly 0.55x0.45x0.5, and I'm placing a gun ring base near z -1.6.

I'm positioning rear drums at z -2.3, x ±0.62 with small radius, checking they clear the barrel and crates. Bed walls stay at interior x ±0.9 with cyan neon strips along the inner rails, and I'm adding a holographic screen plane with an SVG texture near the top of the receiver facing rearward for a glowing display effect.

For the weapon itself, I'm placing a shield near the barrel base facing rear with a magenta slit sight, then defining the receiver as a small box with an energy cell glow on top and a barrel made of a thin cylinder with an octagonal shroud section.

Placing the magazine box on the side and adding an ammo belt as small boxes strung along a curved path toward the receiver, then adding yoke arms and a pedestal cylinder to support the gun assembly.

Now I'm setting up the pedestal base and ring flange, and deciding how the pitch and yaw joints organize child parts -- receiver, barrel, magazine, belt, and shield all follow the gun's rotation. I'm also planning a coiled cable using a spiral sweep lying on the floor near the body.

Positioning the coil between the drums, then routing a connecting cable from the coil to the gun base with a catmull sweep. For materials, I'm giving the floor a panelled iron finish, applying worn paint to the hull, and mottling the crate's surface color.

Now I'm adding a stenciled "AMMO 7.62" decal to the crate's rear and side faces, plus yellow strap boxes wrapping slightly larger than the crate near the top. For the drums I'm considering a lathed or 8-sided cylinder shape with hazard markings.

Adding roll bar rods and braces...

Now I'm planning neon accent strips along the bed floor edges and tailgate, plus starting on the holographic screen element.

I'm thinking through where to mount the holo screen with cyan glowing graphics on a dark panel, attaching it near the gun pitch assembly via a small arm rod, and sketching out the ammo box details before moving to code. I'm setting up a geometry cache helper for reusable box shapes.

Now I'm adding a cylinder helper, planning additional textures like a stencil crate pattern and a serial label, plus hazard stripe decals along the floor edge using thin painted boxes. I'm also laying out floor ribs as repeated box segments spaced across the rear of the floor.
